points.text: Prophet Ayyub (a.s) was a descendant of Ibraheem (a.s). He was immensely blessed with good health and strength. He was wealthy, having large plots of land, abundant livestock and a righteous and beautiful family. Moreover, he was a community leader who was highly respected and loved by his people. He constantly thanked and glorified Allah for everything he was blessed with.

Allah tested Ayyub (a.s), wherein first his wealth began to diminish. His land, livestock, servants and money slowly evaded him until he was left with nothing. Then Allah took away all his children (it is believed that he had 14 children and all of them died). He then became sick, so much so that the skin of his body used to fall off revealing his muscles and bones. While all this happened, he never allowed himself to complain to Allah or to falter in his belief.

His relatives, friends and everyone who loved him and respected him left Ayyub except for his wife who would take care of him. With no money and no income, his wife took up a job to provide for him. But the people of the city did not allow his wife to work for long, since they feared that she would afflict them with the same illness as Ayyub was suffering.

One day his wife approached Ayyub complaining of the situation and said: “You are the Prophet and the messenger of Allah. You have the closest relationship to Allah. Ask Allah to take you out of this harm that you are in!”

Ayyub (a.s) replied saying: “Shaitaan must have whispered in your ears and made you dissatisfied”. He asked her as to how long he enjoyed good health and riches; to which she replied eighty or so years. He then asked for how long he has been suffering like this, and she responded that it was seven years.

Ayyub then said that he felt ashamed to plead to his Rabb to remove his afflictions, for he has not suffered longer than the years of good health and plenty that Allah had provided to him and his family. Feeling that the faith of his wife had weakened and she was dissatisfied with the will of Allah, Ayyub swore that whenever he would regain his health, he will punish her with a hundred lashes. From that day, Ayyub did not eat or drink through his wife’s hand and asked that he be left alone.

Feeling helpless, Ayyub turned to Allah seeking His mercy which are captured beautifully in the Quranic Aayat below. Allah cured Ayyub (a.s) from his affliction through a spring of water gushing forth from his feet.

Ayyub regained his health and his strength. It happened so quickly that his wife did not recognize Ayyub when she saw him in a state of good health. They re-united together and Allah showed an easy way to Ayyub to keep his promise. Allah then gave him more wealth than what he previously had and blessed him with more children than before.

The story of Ayyub (a.s) captures the essence of dealing with adversity and it is through patience, firm faith and gratitude to your Rabb. His faith remained rock solid in the face of most challenging times, which is what made him a remarkable being and Allah calls him to be a person full of patience and an excellent devotee.

verses.text: Mention is made of Ayub (a.s) (or Job) who called upon Allah (while in extreme sickness) saying, “Shaitaan has affl  icted me with distress and suff ering”. (Surah S’ad : Section 4)
Allah said to him, “Strike your foot on the ground. A cool spring will gush forth. Wash and drink to refresh yourself”. (Surah S’ad : Section 4)
Allah then restored him to his family and more, as a grace from Himself and as a reminder to the people of understanding. (Surah S’ad : Section 4)

(At the time of his prolonged illness, his wife had lost patience and complained to him about Allah. Ayub (a.s) became upset with her and promised to give her one hundred strikes (or lashes) once he recovered) (Surah S’ad : Section 4)
(Allah showed him an easy way out), wherein Allah said: “Take a bunch of twigs and strike with it and do not break your oath.” (Surah S’ad : Section 4)
Certainly Allah found Ayub (a.s) full of patience and he was an excellent devotee, who turned to Allah over and over again. (Surah S’ad : Section 4)
Similarly We blessed Ayub, when he prayed to his Rabb saying: “I am badly afflicted with distress; but of all those who show mercy, You are the most Merciful”. (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 6)

We accepted his prayer and relieved his affliction, and restored not only his family but also as many more with them as a favor from Us so that it may serve as a reminder to Our worshippers. (Surah Al-Anbiya : Section 6)
